How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is everything you’ll need to hit the **“Get Information of an Interface”** endpoint on your Cisco Nexus‑Dashboard appliance running v6.3.1 at `192.120.45.67`.

---

### 1️⃣ Endpoint Overview  

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Base URL | `https://<dashboard-ip>` |
| Full Path | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` |

> **Note:**  
> * All calls require HTTPS.  
> * Authentication is done via a bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>`).  
> * If you’re testing locally, you may also add `--insecure` to skip certificate validation.

---

### 2️⃣ Query Parameters (exact names & allowed values)

```text
fabricName      – Name of the Fabric   → “Network1”
nodeId          – Node ID              → 12
podId           – Pod ID               → 10
interfaceType   – Type of interface    → ethernet        (case‑insensitive)
infoType        – Info requested       → speed
```

*Allowed enum values:*  
- `interfaceType`: `"gigabitethernet"` | `"fastethernet"` | `"ethernet"` | `"serial"`
- `infoType`: `"statistics"` | `"status"` | `"config"` | `"speed"`

*(Your input used capitalized words; the API expects lower‑case strings.)*

---

### 3️⃣ Constructed Request URL

Putting it all together:

```
https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?\
fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=speed
```

---

### 4️⃣ Example Calls

#### A) Using **cURL**

```bash
curl -k \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE" \
  "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?" \
  --data-urlencode "fabricName=Network1" \
  --data-urlencode "nodeId=12" \
  --data-urlencode "podId=10" \
  --data-urlencode "interfaceType=ethernet" \
  --data-urlencode "infoType=speed"
```

> Replace `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN_HERE` with the JWT / OAuth token issued by the dashboard.

#### B) Using **Python requests** (quick demo)

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo"

payload = {
    "fabricName": "Network1",
    "nodeId": 12,
    "podId": 10,
    "interfaceType": "ethernet",   # <-- lower-case!
    "infoType": "speed"
}

headers = {
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {your_token}"
}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, params=payload, headers=headers, verify=False)  # verify=False skips cert check

print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())
```

> **Tip:** In production always set `verify=True` and supply a proper CA bundle.

---

### 5️⃣ What You Get Back

A successful call returns JSON similar to:

```json
{
  "fabricName":"Network1",
  "nodeId":12,
  "podId":10,
  "interfaces":[
    {
      "name":"Ethernet0/1",
      "type":"ethernet",
      "speedMbps":10000
    }
  ]
}
```

If no matching interfaces exist, you’ll receive an empty list or a 404 status depending on configuration.

---

### 6️⃣ Common Pitfalls

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| HTTP 401 Unauthorized | Wrong/missing token | Verify token scope & expiry |
| HTTP 400 Bad Request | Parameter typo or wrong value | Double‑check spelling & casing |
| Empty result set | No such interface exists | Confirm interface actually exists on node/pod/fabric |
| SSL error | Self‑signed cert not trusted | Add `--cacert` or `verify=False` during dev |

---

That’s all! With this URL + header combo you can pull the current speed statistics for any Ethernet port on any node within the specified fabric. Happy querying!
